column3: D6 and D2 task success now obeys the same spread rule as every other number
column4: report.py's compare() has refused a token difference smaller than the within-config spread since the first version, but the pass-count block below it compared raw totals and announced that "the post's prescription held" on a one-task difference. A single pass count per config cannot be inconclusive because there is nothing to vary against, so trial_pass_counts() groups passes by trial and gives task success a spread of its own. D2 is the same defect seen from the README: it claimed the suite covered "the report refusing to state a difference smaller than its own spread" while no gate ran report.py at all.

column3: C9 state is resolved from the shell cwd, not the project root
column4: Found live rather than by review: this session's own occupancy monitor hit amber while the shell had drifted into tests/fixtures/transcripts, and wrote the handoff manifest and its acted marker under that directory. A session starting from the repo root will never find that manifest, so the resume path silently misses any handoff written from a subdirectory, and the acted marker fails to suppress a repeat. column3: C1 a hash inside a fenced block is a shell comment, not a heading
column4: patch.py already had fence_mask and used it; extract.py and budget.py did not, so the same file parsed into different sections depending on which script read it, and a token figure could be priced against a boundary /apply would not agree with. The board recorded C1 against all three scripts; it was real for two. One fence-aware parser now lives in cdlib and all three import it. Measured before fixing: Ben's current CLAUDE.md has zero lines inside a fence that start with a hash, so this was latent on his machine and live for anyone else.
column5: Verified: new gate section_targeting_is_unambiguous proves no shell comment becomes a heading and that budget.py and extract.py agree on the section count.

column3: C2 a heading is not a unique key, at either end
column4: extract.py hashed the crumb plus the heading, and the crumb already ends with that heading, so two identically named sections under one parent got the same id. Fixing the id alone would not have helped: patch.py cut by heading text and took the first match, so the plan could not name the second one even with unique ids. section_id now includes a 1-based occurrence ordinal, which unlike a line number does not churn when unrelated text above is edited; extract.py emits that ordinal; and cut_section refuses an ambiguous heading outright rather than guessing, because silently cutting the wrong section is the worst outcome an edit path can have.
column5: Verified on a fixture with three "### Notes", two of them sharing a full crumb: ambiguous heading refused with a reason, occurrence 2 and 3 cut the right sections, an unambiguous heading still cuts with no occurrence, and a fenced line is not cuttable. 36 gates pass.

column3: H3 the occupancy tail now grows until it finds a usage record
column4: last_usage read a single fixed 512 KB tail. One large trailing record, a big tool result or a long assistant turn, pushed the last assistant usage out of that window and the monitor returned nothing. The failure is silent and it lands exactly when a session is at its largest, which is the only time occupancy matters. The tail now starts at 512 KB and grows eightfold until it finds one, bounded at 16 MB so a pathological file cannot stall a 50 ms hook. Split into _usage_in so the caller can tell "not in this window" from "not anywhere"; my first version returned an empty pair for both and the window never grew, which the test caught.

column3: D3 the 200 ms hook claim now names the unit it is true in
column4: The README said the gate suite checked an under-200 ms hook cost per session. No gate bounded any total, and the Stop bound alone permits two seconds. Measuring it showed the claim was against the wrong unit as well: one of every hook costs about 390 ms, but five hooks never fire together, and a bare python3 -c pass is 30 to 40 ms here, so five processes spend roughly 175 ms on interpreter startup alone. A per-session 200 ms is unreachable by construction and a session with a hundred tool calls pays the monitor a hundred times. The gate now bounds the hooks that fire on one event, which is what a user actually waits for.
column5: Verified: worst event is PreCompact at about 140 ms across one hook, budget 200. README rewritten to state per-event and to say plainly that a per-session total is not a claim this plugin makes.

column3: the compact directive's mechanism reproduces on this machine, so it is deleted
column4: Part 12.1 requires reproducing the pricing claim before acting on it. The multipliers are published rates and cannot be read off a transcript, but the mechanism can. Across 413 transcripts: an ordinary turn above 20,000 prefix tokens has a median cache_creation of 1,371 against a median cache_read of 284,209, while the turn immediately after a compaction has 90,337 against 34,068. Creation exceeds read on 38 of 44 post-compaction turns (86%) against 1,563 of 34,966 ordinary ones (4.5%).
column5: A compaction moves roughly 89,000 tokens per turn from the read price to the write price. The direction holds at any cache pricing, because a read costing less than a write is the entire point of caching. occupancy_monitor.py:185 no longer asks for a compaction; both bands still write and verify the manifest and report. Gate monitor_never_asks_for_compaction checks both bands and the shipped source, because a directive re-added on a path no fixture reaches would pass a behavioural check alone.

column3: the monitor now watches the cache, which is the quantity with a price on it
column4: The band system watched fullness. A cold turn at 12 percent occupancy costs real money and produced nothing at all, because occupancy was the wrong quantity to watch. cache_state() and hit_ratio() are ported from the v4 source. resolve_window is deliberately not taken: this build's measured compaction ceiling is better evidence than its hard-coded 1,000,000.
column5: Confirmed live on the session that wrote this row: the new signal fired with 320,843 tokens re-processed at the write price against 0 read. Gate cold_cache_turn_is_reported pairs the cold fixture with a warm one of the same size, so a hook that shouted on every turn would fail it rather than pass.
